final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic swap in the head domain: maximal ESM-1v plausibility (1.0), favorable ProteinMPNN delta (-1.52), and Ile tolerated in ~10% of homologs. Conservative surface/core-preserving change is the safest bet for retaining or enhancing G-F triggering and entry efficiency.

Backup conservative hydrophobic substitution at the same best-supported position; beta-branched Val may pack slightly differently but remains physicochemically conservative. Expected to preserve receptor-binding and fusion-triggering geometry.
Ser is a small, physicochemically conservative replacement for Asn at a solvent-exposed position, less disruptive than the rejected N324Q. Modest confidence given no direct functional readout.

stop_reason.detail: No tool measures the entry-efficiency phenotype directly; existing viability-proxy evidence already gives a stable, well-separated Top-3, so extra rounds would not change the decision.

history.rationale: Removes a predicted N-linked glycosylation site (N324-L325-S326 motif); glycan trimming in the G head can increase F-triggering kinetics and fusion. Gln is the conservative, chemically similar substitution.

N324 is a surface-exposed residue in the globular head; deglycosylation-like Asn→Gln changes in NiV/HeV G can alter receptor engagement and F-triggering without destroying the fold. Retained pending MSA/PLM evidence.
Weakened: mediocre ESM-1v plausibility (0.48), unfavorable ProteinMPNN delta (-4.36, high B-factor region), and Gln nearly absent in homologs (4.8%) — demote below L343I.
Highly conservative branched-chain substitution in the head domain; low-risk baseline candidate to calibrate plausibility tools.
Conservative Leu→Ile in the head domain is unlikely to disrupt structure but offers only weak rationale for improved entry; kept as a low-priority baseline.

Strongest profile: maximal ESM-1v plausibility (1.0), favorable ProteinMPNN delta (-1.52, B-factor 35.6), and Ile observed in ~10% of homologs — a conservative hydrophobic change unlikely to disrupt receptor binding or F-triggering.
Same solvent-exposed position as N324Q but Ser is smaller and closer to Asn physicochemically; hypothesis that it preserves structure compatibility better than Gln.
Alternative conservative hydrophobic swap at the best-supported position 343; Val is beta-branched and may pack slightly better, providing a backup near the top candidate.
